title: How AI is Reshaping Semiconductor Design and Manufacturing
gist: Summarizing an Intel Foundry presentation at the GSA European Executive Forum, the piece argues AI scaling needs power delivery, packaging, connectivity and resilient supply chains, and that Intel uses AI in manufacturing for defect detection and yield learning. It is largely promotional.

insights.claim: Agentic AI creates less predictable multistep reasoning workloads, making efficient power delivery and high-performance connectivity essential to scale.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Power delivery and interconnect are the bottlenecks to watch.

insights.claim: Physical AI at the edge requires architectures balancing capability, efficiency and cost, supported by automation and modeling to improve manufacturing yield.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Edge AI favors cost-efficient nodes and yield learning.

insights.claim: Sovereign AI makes where chips are made a requirement, and Intel Foundry markets capabilities across North America, Europe and Asia as geographically diverse and resilient.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Supply chain location is a selling point for Intel Foundry with government-aligned customers.

insights.claim: Intel 18A uses RibbonFET gate-all-around transistors and PowerVia backside power, reducing resistance, voltage drop and power delivery noise, combined with high-density MIM capacitors.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Backside power is a differentiator versus TSMC's near-term nodes.

insights.claim: Intel Foundry balances backside power complexity with frontside lower-metal pitches allowing direct-print patterning to manage manufacturing cost.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: EMIB-T integrates power transfer into its bridge and can remove the need for a full silicon interposer in many applications, while Foveros Direct uses hybrid bonding to stack compute dies on base dies.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Advanced packaging is a foundry growth lever against interposer-based approaches.

insights.claim: Chiplet architectures with UCIe standardized die-to-die links let designers combine specialized dies, memory stacks and accelerators instead of integrating everything on one chip.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Chiplet standardization widens the foundry and packaging ecosystem.

insights.claim: Intel Foundry fabs collect nearly a billion images each week, and machine learning analyzes them to detect defects, classify failure patterns, flag yield risks and improve design rules.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Data scale supports faster yield learning on 18A.
insights.locator: nearly a billion images each week

insights.claim: Neural networks and ensemble decision trees isolate root causes, giving faster learning cycles and more predictable yield progression as technologies enter production.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Yield ramp predictability matters for foundry customer trust.
insights.locator: Neural networks and ensemble decision trees

insights.claim: Digital twins and predictive maintenance monitor equipment to catch tool issues before they disrupt production.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: AI assists design technology co-optimization by exploring large design spaces and power, performance and area tradeoffs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
